test_title: SSC CGL Tier-II ( JSO ) 2021 Official Paper ( Held On: 10 August 2022 )
subject: general
question: For frequency distribution presentation, which option is wrong?

options.text: In a histogram, a bar is created above each score (or class interval) so that the height of the bar corresponds to the frequency
Bar graph presents score categories that are measured from a nominal or an ordinal scale
The smooth curve emphasizes the fact that the distribution is not showing the exact frequency for each category.
In a polygon, an additional line is not drawn at each to bring the graph back to a zero frequency

solution:
The correct answer is** in a polygon, an additional line is not drawn at each to bring the graph back to a zero frequency.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A frequency polygon is a line graph that plots class frequency against the class midpoint. You can get it by connecting the midpoints of the rectangles' tops in the histogram.
 
• One must include the first and last class with zero frequencies in order to confirm that our graph is genuinely a polygon (i.e., the graph is closed-shape). Draw attention to the frequency column and the column with the midpoints for each class. 

*** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__***

 
• A histogram is a bar graph with rectangle-shaped bars displaying the data, but a frequency polygon is a line graph with a curved line showing the data. 
 
• A polygon has flat surfaces throughout. A polygon must have a minimum of three sides. Each side of a line segment must intersect another line segment only at its terminal. By counting the sides of a polygon, we may quickly ascertain its geometry. 

**Hence, f*or frequency distribution presentation, the wrong option is in a polygon, an additional line is not drawn at each to bring the graph back to a zero frequency.***
